clock_dir_to: Croatian SUBTRACTIVE clock direction: "do" ("to/until") names the minutes
still missing from the coming hour -- "petnaest do devet" == fifteen to
nine == 08:45, "četvrt do devet" == a quarter to nine == 08:45.  This is
the ordinary "to" reading (subtract from the named hour), NOT the
"to, until, up to" with the genitive.  The clock use with a worked
numeric example is in hjp.znanje.hr, s.v. "četvrt": "četvrt do devet"
clock_fraction_15: Croatian QUARTER hour.  Unlike "pola" (which counts toward the coming
hour, 08:30 for "pola devet"), the quarter is only ever spoken with an
explicit direction word -- "četvrt do devet" == 08:45 -- so
``bare_quarter_to`` is deliberately NOT set for hr and a bare
"četvrt devet" stays unparsed rather than guessed.
"četvrtina sata; petnaest minuta", with the clock example
clock_fraction_30: Croatian toward-hour HALF: "pola devet" == half toward the ninth == 08:30
(bare_half_to + toward_hour_12h).  Unlike Czech/Slovak, the half names the
coming hour with the bare CARDINAL, not an ordinal.  Citations, both with
a worked numeric example naming the SAME hour ("half past one" = 1:30):
past one" == 1:30): "Serbo-Croatian: pola dva (used with the following
hour)" -- "dva" (two) is the COMING hour, confirming the same

marker_ad: The Hrvatski jezični portal entry for "p. Kr." glosses it "poslije Krista"
and gives "n. e." as its alternative
Hrvatski pravopis writes the same abbreviation "po. Kr."
marker_bc: Croatian has two live pairs. The Hrvatski pravopis of the Institut za
hrvatski jezik i jezikoslovlje prescribes "pr. Kr." for "prije Krista"
entry for it names "pr. n. e." (prije nove ere) as the secular equivalent
marker_day_filler: Croatian idiom: a bare genitive-plural "dana" (of days) trailing a
year/month/week count is the emphatic filler "godinu/mjesec/tjedan DANA"
(literally "a year/month/week OF DAYS" == exactly one year/month/week),
never a genuine extra day -- a standalone "+1 day" reads the nominative
"dan", not this genitive-plural form.  Institut za hrvatski jezik /
Hrvatski jezični portal, sklonidba imenice "dan": genitiv množine "dana".
marker_for_date: "za" + accusative marks the time a thing is meant for: "za sutra", "za petak".
accusative]", "doći kući za praznike" (to come home for the holiday season).
marker_last: Croatian "last/previous" determiner, the full adjectival paradigm.  Croatian
names a past year with the adverbial genitive "prošle godine" and a past week
with either the accusative "prošli tjedan" or the genitive "prošlog tjedna",
so the nominative-only listing missed the commonest phrasings.  The masculine
genitive/dative have the attested short and long variants (-og / -oga,
-om / -ome).  The season nouns are neuter, so "prošlo ljeto" and
"prethodno proljeće" need the neuter nominative/accusative too.
marker_next: Croatian "next/following" determiner, the full adjectival paradigm for both
the "sljedeći" and the "idući" stems, including the -eg/-ega and -em/-emu
variants.  "sljedeće godine" (genitive) is the ordinary "next year".
Institut za hrvatski jezik / Hrvatski jezični portal, sklonidba pridjeva.
marker_ordlast: "posljednji ponedjeljak svibnja" = last Monday of May.  IHJ, Hrvatski pravopis.
marker_this: Croatian "this" demonstrative, the full pronominal paradigm; "ove godine" is
the ordinary "this year" and is genitive.  Institut za hrvatski jezik /

scope_unit_century: The locative singular the "u" preposition takes -- "u 20. stoljeću" ("in the
20th century"), the ordinary way to place an event in a century.  Distinct
from the genitive plural "stoljeća" a bare count uses ("pet stoljeća"), so
admitting it cannot admit a count.
Hrvatski jezicni portal, stoljece, sklonidba (lokativ jd. "stoljecu").
